key_idea: Count non-crossing spanning trees of points on a circle with an allowed-edge matrix using interval DP with two tables: trees on [i..j], and trees on [i..j] that contain the edge i-j.
sketch: ok[i][j] = gcd(x_i,x_j)>1. Let g[i][j] be the number of non-crossing spanning trees on vertices i..j and f[i][j] the number of those that use edge (i,j). Removing edge (i,j) splits the tree into a tree on i..k and a tree on k+1..j, so f[i][j] = ok * sum_k g[i][k]*g[k+1][j]. For g, take k as the farthest neighbour of i: g[i][j] = sum_{k>i} f[i][k]*g[k][j], which is unambiguous so nothing is double counted. Answer g[0][n-1] mod 1e9+7; O(n^3) = 2.7e7. The circle needs no special treatment because edge (0,n-1) is just another chord. Verified against subset enumeration for n<=7.
